# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_002_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 1, Chapter 2

**1** After she had said these things to me she fell silent, and I saw her no more. I was seized with trembling and grief. I said to myself, "If this sin is reckoned against me, how can I be saved? Or how shall I propitiate God for my great and grievous sins? With what words shall I ask the Lord to be merciful to me?" **2** While I was deliberating these things and reasoning about them in my heart, I saw before me a great white chair made of snow-white wool; and there came an aged woman in shining garments, holding a book in her hands. She sat down alone and greeted me: "Greetings, Hermas." **3** And I, in grief and weeping, said: "Greetings, lady." And she said to me, "Why are you gloomy, Hermas? You who are patient and good-tempered and who always smiles — why are you downcast in countenance and not cheerful?" **4** And I said to her, "Because of an excellent woman who says that I have sinned against her." And she said, "Far be such a thing from a servant of God! Nevertheless, the thought concerning her did arise in your heart. It is such a thing as this that brings sin upon the servants of God. For it is a wicked and ruinous intention, when one who is righteous desires a wicked deed; and most of all when Hermas the temperate, who abstains from every evil desire, does it, and desires a wicked desire." **5** "But God is not wrathful for this reason only, but that you may convert your household, who have sinned against the Lord and against you their parents. And although you are fond of your children, yet you did not admonish your household, but allowed it to become greatly corrupted. Therefore the Lord is wrathful with you. But he will heal all the past evils in your household, for on account of their sins and iniquities you have been consumed by the cares of this life. **6** But the great mercy of the Lord has taken pity on you and your household, and will strengthen you, and establish you in his glory. Only do not be idle, but be of good courage and strengthen your household. For just as a smith hammers out his work, so the daily use of righteousness will overcome all wickedness. Therefore do not cease admonishing your children; for I know that if they repent with all their heart, they will be enrolled in the books of life with the saints."

---

*EMET note: The "great white chair" renders the precise description of the throne; "snow-white wool" is literal. The aged woman is the personified Church, not yet identified.*
